quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane next to the solid yellow line.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can cross the broken line to pass. You cannot cross the solid line to pass.

questions.question: Dust or smoke is blocking your view of other vehicles. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Turn on your parking lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights anytime you cannot see other vehicles clearly. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: You are turning left from a one-way street with multiple lanes onto another one-way street. Which lane should you start from?

options.text: Any lane, as long as it is safe.
The lane closest to the left curb.
The center lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street to another one-way street, start your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: How can you help the driver behind you stay a safe distance away?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Drive at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Maintain a steady speed and signal your turns, lane changes, and slowing down. This helps the driver behind you stay a safe distance away.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this road sign?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is starting. You should keep to the right.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and stop if cars are coming.
Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.
Go through the intersection slowly, not always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk or at a point where you can see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are to your left and parked vehicles are to your right. Which way should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles.
Between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: When oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right, steer down the middle between them.

questions.question: Pedestrians are crossing the street illegally, not at a crosswalk. Must you stop for them?

options.text: Yes, you must stop for them.
No, you do not have to stop.
You should honk your horn instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: Bad weather or dim light requires you to use your lights while driving. Which lights should you use?

options.text: Parking lights.
High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams create glare by reflecting off the moisture and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Watch for other drivers trying to enter the same lane. Never change lanes in an intersection.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To prevent hydroplaning in rain, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down in rain to reduce hydroplaning risk. Driving too fast causes your tires to float on water and lose contact with the road. This makes your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off water and snow, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard to stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Brake gently and smoothly to stop your vehicle gradually.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass a car:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
Never.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver won't expect you there and may pull off the road.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is coming with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Pull over to the side and stop.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Try to reach your destination before it catches you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, pull over to the right side of the road and stop completely. Do not try to outrun it.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and hazmat trucks.
Watch for multiple trains.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: Be very careful at railroad crossings. Only cross when sure no train is coming. Watch for school buses and hazmat trucks that must stop at all crossings.

questions.question: When using a roundabout, drivers should:

options.text: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Yield to traffic entering.
Drive clockwise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: In a roundabout, traffic moves counterclockwise around a central island. Drivers entering must yield to traffic already in the roundabout, then follow the circle right to their exit.

questions.question: Driving slower than surrounding traffic is:

options.text: Good if the weather is bad.
Okay if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because other drivers may try to pass unsafely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because other drivers may try to pass unsafely.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than traffic can be dangerous. Frustrated drivers may take unsafe risks to pass you.

questions.question: The proper way to make a right turn is to:

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the center before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach in the right lane, then move toward the center before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal before turning to warn other drivers. Slow down and stay as close as possible to the right curb when approaching the intersection.

questions.question: Your reaction time becomes slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your ability to see clearly and makes you less alert. As you drink more alcohol, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and how fast other vehicles are moving.

questions.question: Which statement is true about taking medications and driving?

options.text: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications cannot affect driving ability when taken as directed.
Medications are always safe to take if a doctor prescribes them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications—prescription or over-the-counter—can be dangerous and may affect your driving. Cold and allergy medications can make you drowsy and hurt your driving ability. You must know how your medication affects your ability to drive.

questions.question: A red painted curb means:

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers only.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red-painted curb.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Stare straight ahead at the road in front.
Only focus on the middle of the road.
Watch to the side, ahead, and behind their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch to the side, ahead, and behind their car.
questions.explanation: A driver should watch to the side, ahead, and behind their car. Good drivers must know what is happening all around their vehicle.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign forbids right turns. You cannot turn right at an intersection where this sign is posted.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic on the road (as long as it follows the speed limit). Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Crashes often happen when some vehicles drive faster or slower than others.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Only the left outside mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Stop before crossing the intersection.
Slow down and go carefully.
Wait for a green light before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look for cross traffic, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: If other cars keep passing you on both sides while you drive in the center lane of an expressway, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On roads with four or more lanes and two-way traffic, drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. On an interstate highway, use the right lane if you are driving slower than the traffic flow.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow down to no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: A school bus turns on flashing red lights and a stop arm when it stops to pick up or drop off students. You must stop and cannot go until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes back in. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You should use cruise control near railroad crossings to keep a steady speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal tells you to. Always drive carefully near railroad tracks.

questions.question: What happens to stopping distances and crash severity as speed increases?

options.text: They decrease.
They stay the same.
They increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase.
questions.explanation: High speeds are dangerous. As your speed increases, it takes longer to stop and crashes become more serious. Serious injury and death are more likely. Leave more space between you and other cars when you drive faster.

questions.question: In a car on a highway, is it legal to drink alcohol?

options.text: No. You cannot drink or have open alcohol containers in a car.
Yes, if you are not the driver.
Yes, if the driver is not drunk.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. You cannot drink or have open alcohol containers in a car.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of alcohol. Drivers and passengers cannot have open alcohol containers in a running vehicle.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance or acceleration ramp, what should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way.
You should let drivers already on the highway go first.
You can force your way into traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should let drivers already on the highway go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a highway from a ramp, yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when you have a clear opening.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all areas behind your car. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to see the blind spots that mirrors cannot show.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Make changes in speed and direction slowly and carefully.
Drive the same way as normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make changes in speed and direction slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make all speed and direction changes slowly. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may slip and you will lose control.

questions.question: When driving behind another car at night, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your headlights on low beam.
Use high beams until you are within 10 feet of the car ahead.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on low beam.
questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are near. Switch to low beams when you are close behind another driver.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beam headlights in fog or mist?

options.text: The light reflects back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles might not see you.
Cars behind you may follow too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light reflects back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, do not use high beams because the light bounces back at you.

questions.question: On a slippery road, what following distance should you keep?

options.text: The same as normal.
Farther than normal.
Closer than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther than normal.
questions.explanation: It takes longer to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Keep extra space between you and the car ahead.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Let all traffic go first before crossing.
Stop, then go when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: You must use your low beams when you are:

options.text: On a lit street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beam light bounces off water and creates glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area for road construction workers.
The area where pedestrians can cross the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians can cross the road.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are areas where pedestrians cross the road. They are often marked with white lines. Some crosswalks have extra lines between them. Some crosswalks have no markings.

questions.question: Night driving is harder because:

options.text: Speed limits are higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the roads at night.
It is hard to judge how far away things are and how fast other cars are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge how far away things are and how fast other cars are going.
questions.explanation: Night driving is difficult because you can only see as far as your headlights reach. This makes it hard to judge distance and the speed of other vehicles.

questions.question: When daylight starts to fade, you should turn on your:

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
Emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams as daylight fades so others can see you. Only use high beams when driving alone in an open area with no other vehicles.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
At the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of traffic already on the road.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when a traffic light turns yellow. You should:

options.text: Slow down and go through the intersection without caution.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will turn red soon. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop, cross the intersection carefully.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You must always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic going straight. Drivers must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station.
Signal before going further.
Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead. It tells you to slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when it is safe.
Check for cars and slow to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up and merge smoothly with traffic. Do not stop like you would on other roads.

questions.question: You may pass a vehicle when:

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can change lanes. A broken yellow line next to your lane means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. Only change lanes when it is safe.
